title: My Reading Week
focus: Present simple; days of the week
paragraphs: Monday. Today is the start of our school reading challenge. We read for twenty minutes every day. I choose a book about dinosaurs.
Tuesday. I read in the school library at break. The book is great! There is a big dinosaur with a long neck. My friend Lía reads a book about space.
Wednesday. I'm tired and I don't want to read. But my dad says, 'Read just ten minutes.' I read fifteen!
Thursday. I finish the dinosaur book. Now I want a book about animals in the sea. Friday. The teacher gives me a gold star. I read every day this week. Reading is fun!

title: Welcome to the Blue Ocean Aquarium
focus: There is / there are; imperatives; times
paragraphs: Welcome to the Blue Ocean Aquarium! See more than two hundred sea animals from around the world. We are open every day, from 9:00 to 5:00.
In the big tank, there are sharks, turtles and colourful fish. Our dolphins do a show at 11:00 and at 3:00. In the touch pool, you can touch a starfish. Please be gentle.
Feeding times: penguins at 10:00 and sharks at 1:00. Children love it!
Tickets: adults $10, children $5, babies free. Don't use flash when you take photos. Don't feed the animals. The gift shop is near the exit. Come and meet our sea friends!

title: My Mum Is a Pilot
paragraphs: My mum, Carolina, is a pilot. She flies big planes from Bogotá to Miami and Madrid. She likes her job because she sees many cities.
Mum gets up at four o'clock on flight days. She puts on her blue uniform and takes her bag. She checks the weather and the plane with another pilot. Then she says 'Welcome!' to the passengers.
She is often away from home. When she is away, she calls us every evening. She brings small presents from different countries.
When Mum is at home, we cook and watch films together. She can't fly when she is tired, so she sleeps a lot! I'm proud of her. One day, I want to be a pilot, too.

title: The Magic Pencil
focus: Present simple; there is / there are
paragraphs: Nina is eight years old and she loves drawing. One day, she finds a golden pencil under her bed. It is small and shiny.
Nina draws an apple. Suddenly, the apple is real! It is red and sweet. 'Wow!' she says. 'A magic pencil!'
She draws a big ice cream. She draws a small dog. But she is careful: she doesn't draw a lion. 'A lion is dangerous,' she thinks. 'I only draw nice things.'
Nina draws a door on her bedroom wall. She opens it and... she is in a beautiful garden! There are blue flowers and birds with golden wings. Nina smiles. 'This is my secret place,' she says.

title: An Email from My Cousin in Spain
paragraphs: Hi Carlos! This is your cousin Rafa from Seville, in Spain. Mum says you are twelve, like me!
I live in a flat near the river with my parents and my grandma. My school is ten minutes from my flat. I walk there with my friend Hugo.
In Spain, people have lunch at about two o'clock and dinner at nine. It's very late! At school we have lunch at one thirty. In the afternoon, I play football in the street with my friends.
What is your day like in Colombia? What time is dinner? Do you have a big family? Send me an email soon! Your cousin, Rafa

title: Dance Classes for Kids
focus: Days of the week; present simple; prices
paragraphs: DANCE CLASSES FOR KIDS! Do you like music? Do you like to move? Come to Baila Conmigo, the dance school on Calle 15.
We have classes for children from six to twelve. On Mondays and Wednesdays, we teach salsa. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, we teach hip hop. On Saturdays, there is a free class for beginners.
Classes are 45 minutes long and cost $20 a month. The first class is free. Wear comfortable clothes and bring a bottle of water. You don't need dancing shoes.
Our teachers are young and friendly. You can watch your child's class through the big window. Call Marisol on 555 0188 or visit us any afternoon from 3:00 to 7:00.

title: What's in My Lunch Box?
focus: Food vocabulary; there is / there are; some / any
paragraphs: Hello, everyone! Today I'm showing you my lunch box. I'm Elisa and I'm in the healthy-food club at school.
In my lunch box, there is a sandwich with chicken and lettuce. There is also an apple, some carrots and a small bottle of water. I don't bring fizzy drinks or crisps. They aren't good for me.
On Fridays, my lunch box has a treat: two small biscuits. I love them! My best friend Ari has a different lunch. He brings rice, beans and an egg. It looks great!
A healthy lunch gives you energy for the afternoon. What is in your lunch box? Are you hungry now? I am!

title: Parque de la Paz: Park Rules
paragraphs: Parque de la Paz – Park Rules. Welcome! The park is open every day from 6:00 in the morning to 8:00 in the evening.
You can walk, run and ride your bike on the green path. You can play football on the big field. You can have a picnic under the trees, but please take your rubbish home.
You can't walk on the flowers. You can't light a fire. You can't play loud music. Dogs are welcome, but keep them on a lead. Please clean up after your dog.
There are toilets near the main gate and a water fountain in the middle of the park. For emergencies, call the guard on 555 0100. Enjoy the park!
